free_tier.stated: No free tier. VPS - NAT512 is USD 7.50 a year: 512 MB RAM, 5 GB SSD, 1 CPU core on fair use, a /80 IPv6 plus a NAT IPv4 with 20 usable ports and 1 SSH port, 750 GB transfer a month. Sold per location; the NAT768 at USD 10 a year is the only other rung and is out of stock at every location checked.

retention.stated: annual prepay; the terms state 'All services are invoiced 10 days before due date. Unpaid services are suspended 3 days after due date. Unpaid services are terminated 5 days after due date, all data is deleted and cannot be recovered.'

egress.terms: 750 GB transfer a month included on NAT512 and 1024 GB on NAT768, both vendor-stated; nothing is published about what happens past the allowance

interface_detail: KVM guest with root over SSH; the NAT IPv4 ports and the public IPv4 are listed in the control panel's Network tab, and a knowledge-base article walks through finding them. No panel for changing the mapping is documented: the ports are assigned, not chosen.
tooling: any SSH client; the vendor's own FAQ recommends 'road warrior WireGuard-installer script for easy setup'
chaining: 512 MB and 5 GB for USD 0.625 a month is the largest shape found under the dollar line, and the vendor's FAQ answers the WireGuard question in one line: 'Yes, it can!'

limits.value: 20 usable ports on a shared NAT IPv4 plus 1 SSH port; the ports are assigned by the provider, not configured by the buyer
annual prepay only at this rung: USD 7.50 is the first payment and the smallest term

binding_note: 750 GB a month is about 25 GB a day, which a tunnel will not reach but a monitoring host with a chatty probe might; the port count is the second constraint and the price is not one.

identity_cost.detail: email address, password and an image captcha, read from the order form's inputs, which are username, password and captcha only. No card, address, phone or ID field is on the order form; payment is collected after the account exists. No card hold is stated anywhere read. The order page warns 'Turn off your VPN before placing an order'.

reliability_note: the FAQ states 'Due to the low cost nature of service, we cannot provide SLA' and 'We strive to maintain 99.9% uptime at all locations'; the status page showed the Canada and France KVM nodes at 100 percent on 2026-10-24; the provider bars Tor, torrents, crypto mining and port scanning and caps sustained CPU at 50 percent of a core over 24 hours

notes: The biggest shape under the dollar line, and the one whose stock is checkable. USD 7.50 a year is USD 0.625 a month for 512 MB and 5 GB, which is 1.33 times the RAM of the C-Servers row for 1.57 times the monthly rate. Stock was read at seven locations and the NAT512 was in stock at all seven, with the NAT768 out of stock at all seven, which is the useful kind of negative: it says the seller's stock flag is live and specific rather than decorative. The WireGuard question is answered by the vendor in one line on its own home page, which is first-party but is a sentence about capability, not a measurement, and no page states UDP on the forwarded ports. The port mapping is the weak point: the knowledge base tells a buyer to read the port list from the Network tab, and no page describes changing a mapping, so this is a product where the 20 ports are assigned rather than chosen. That is worse than C-Servers for a buyer who needs a specific port and fine for WireGuard, which does not care. Entity: the footer gives 'Registered Name - NatVPS Services' and GSTIN 27LNZPS0316Q1ZQ, whose check digit validates under the GSTIN algorithm and whose state code 27 is Maharashtra, so the registration number is internally consistent; it was not checked against the Indian GST portal, which needs a captcha. The tracker row naming WebHorizon IT Broadband Limited as the owner was not confirmed. Not established: UDP on the forwarded ports, whether the assigned ports can be changed, and the payment rails at checkout, because the gateway list only appears after the account exists.

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 7.50 a year / 12 = USD 0.625 a month, paid in one go. A VPS bills whether it runs or not, so the 24/7 and 10 h/day figures are the same. Annual prepay is the only option at this rung: the billing selector prints one choice.
